Follow the playbook for <project id="9e0670cc-3e1d-43db-bf20-f4118a5d050c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/obsidian-within-lab-dg-collaboration-publish-and-import-9e316a1188b0">Obsidian within-lab DG collaboration (Publish & Import)</project>

>>>

>>> ## Goal

* Enable Roam and Obsidian to both act as source and destination for DB-backed Discourse Graph push-pull sync. MVP0 mirrors the existing Obsidian-to-Obsidian reference behavior: a source app shares one selected node to a group, shared persistence stores the node and required dependencies, and a destination app discovers, imports, and refreshes shared nodes from the other app. Assumes \[\[Project/Sharing group management\]\] is complete
* MVP0 / v0 is:
  * A Roam <-> Supabase <-> Obsidian flow, not a portable-package-first flow.
  * Single-node-share driven, matching the current Obsidian publish command. Import may still select multiple visible shared nodes.
  * Manual share/publish grants group access; already-shared source content stays fresh through each source app's existing local-to-remote sync behavior. Pull/import/refresh remains explicit/manual.
  * Group-targeted. The user chooses a group they belong to when sharing a node, after the separate group-sharing work is available.
  * Cross-app: Roam can source content for Obsidian, Obsidian can source content for Roam, and both apps can import from the other.
  * Markdown-first for content transport. \[\[\[\[ISS\]\] - v0 content model\]\] atJSON is the intended canonical content model, but it is not required for v0.
  * Built on existing Supabase auth, RLS, group access, content, concept, and file-reference tables where possible.

>>>

>>> ## Non-Goals

* MVP0 / v0 is not intended to solve:
  * Real-time bidirectional merge sync or collaborative conflict resolution.
  * Full atJSON storage, API negotiation, or app adapter rollout.
  * A complete portable package implementation.
  * New local persistence models for either app. Obsidian should keep markdown files, frontmatter, imported assets, and ; Roam should keep pages, blocks, and its existing relation representation.
  * Multi-node share as a single source operation. MVP0 share mirrors current Obsidian publish behavior: one node per share action.
  * Full recursive context export. MVP0 should preserve the selected node and required dependencies, not walk the whole reachable graph.
  * Direct sharing to individual users. MVP0 uses group sharing only.
  * Automatic remote-to-local polling or background pull into destination apps.
  * Explicit cross-schema translation, schema-equivalence UI, or automatic merging of incompatible local schemas.
  * Perfect preservation of every Roam or Obsidian formatting edge case.

>>>

>>> ## In-Scope Use Cases

>>> ### UC1: Source user shares one discourse node to a group

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user wants collaborators in another Roam graph or Obsidian vault to access one discourse node.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The user chooses a single discourse node to share.
>   * 2\. The user chooses one or many target group from the groups they belong to.
>   * 3\. The source app collects the selected node, required node schema, markdown content, origin identity, and any relation or asset dependencies valid to share under the Obsidian reference rules.
>   * 4\. The source app ensures the selected node and required dependency records are persisted through the normal local-to-remote sync contract.
>   * 5\. The source app grants access to the chosen group through shared persistence.
>   * 6\. Later local edits to the shared source node are propagated by the existing local-to-remote sync model; the user does not need to re-share unless the target group changes.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC2: Destination user discovers cross-app shared nodes

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user opens an import surface after being granted access to shared content from the other app.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The destination app queries visible shared resources.
>   * 2\. Nodes from the other app appear with source app, source space, title, source-local ID, and modified time.
>   * 3\. Already imported nodes are hidden or marked using stable origin identity.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC3: Obsidian user pulls Roam-origin nodes into a vault

> * **Actor:** Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Roam-origin nodes from the import UI.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The Obsidian plugin fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2\. The plugin materializes each Roam node as a markdown file under an import folder, with mapped , stable , and frontmatter.
>   * 3\. The plugin imports relations where both endpoints resolve locally, then reports import successes and failures.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC4: Roam user pulls Obsidian-origin nodes into a graph

> * **Actor:** Roam user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Obsidian-origin nodes from the Roam import surface.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The Roam extension fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2\. The extension materializes each Obsidian node into Roam using the v0 markdown payload and Roam's markdown import/from-markdown capability.
>     * And changes to existing nodes are overwritten
>   * 3\. The extension stores stable origin identity so the imported node can be recognized and refreshed later.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC5: Destination user refreshes an imported cross-app node

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** An imported node has changed upstream and the destination user explicitly asks for the latest shared version.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The destination app identifies the source app, source space, and source-local node ID from stored origin identity.
>   * 2\. The destination app fetches the latest shared markdown content and metadata.
>   * 3\. The destination app updates the existing imported node without creating a duplicate and refreshes source timestamps.
>   * Any changes to the imported node are overwritten.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC6: Relation between separately shared nodes is preserved

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The source user shares a discourse node that has a stored discourse relation to another node already shared to the same group.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The source app confirms both relation endpoints are shared to the same group.
>   * 2\. The source app writes the relation type schema and relation instance into shared persistence using the same semantic shape Obsidian imports today.
>   * 3\. The destination app maps or creates the local relation type and materializes the relation if both endpoints resolve locally.

{"id":"P-DIS-166","uuid":"18c30753-b874-4691-9877-c5de444f66a2","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian","summary":"Inter-graph: Roam/Obsidian","description":">>> ## Links

* [Roam Project](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/rOBMYfhKh>)
* [Scoping Doc](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/iC568HqDZ>)

* [Quarterly roadmap prioritizing](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/avAAfIthf>) 

Follow the playbook for <project id="9e0670cc-3e1d-43db-bf20-f4118a5d050c" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/obsidian-within-lab-dg-collaboration-publish-and-import-9e316a1188b0">Obsidian within-lab DG collaboration (Publish & Import)</project>

>>>

>>> ## Goal

* Enable Roam and Obsidian to both act as source and destination for DB-backed Discourse Graph push-pull sync. MVP0 mirrors the existing Obsidian-to-Obsidian reference behavior: a source app shares one selected node to a group, shared persistence stores the node and required dependencies, and a destination app discovers, imports, and refreshes shared nodes from the other app. Assumes \[\[Project/Sharing group management\]\] is complete
* MVP0 / v0 is:
  * A Roam <-> Supabase <-> Obsidian flow, not a portable-package-first flow.
  * Single-node-share driven, matching the current Obsidian publish command. Import may still select multiple visible shared nodes.
  * Manual share/publish grants group access; already-shared source content stays fresh through each source app's existing local-to-remote sync behavior. Pull/import/refresh remains explicit/manual.
  * Group-targeted. The user chooses a group they belong to when sharing a node, after the separate group-sharing work is available.
  * Cross-app: Roam can source content for Obsidian, Obsidian can source content for Roam, and both apps can import from the other.
  * Markdown-first for content transport. \[\[\[\[ISS\]\] - v0 content model\]\] atJSON is the intended canonical content model, but it is not required for v0.
  * Built on existing Supabase auth, RLS, group access, content, concept, and file-reference tables where possible.

>>>

>>> ## Non-Goals

* MVP0 / v0 is not intended to solve:
  * Real-time bidirectional merge sync or collaborative conflict resolution.
  * Full atJSON storage, API negotiation, or app adapter rollout.
  * A complete portable package implementation.
  * New local persistence models for either app. Obsidian should keep markdown files, frontmatter, imported assets, and ; Roam should keep pages, blocks, and its existing relation representation.
  * Multi-node share as a single source operation. MVP0 share mirrors current Obsidian publish behavior: one node per share action.
  * Full recursive context export. MVP0 should preserve the selected node and required dependencies, not walk the whole reachable graph.
  * Direct sharing to individual users. MVP0 uses group sharing only.
  * Automatic remote-to-local polling or background pull into destination apps.
  * Explicit cross-schema translation, schema-equivalence UI, or automatic merging of incompatible local schemas.
  * Perfect preservation of every Roam or Obsidian formatting edge case.

>>>

>>> ## In-Scope Use Cases

>>> ### UC1: Source user shares one discourse node to a group

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user wants collaborators in another Roam graph or Obsidian vault to access one discourse node.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The user chooses a single discourse node to share.
>   * 2\. The user chooses one or many target group from the groups they belong to.
>   * 3\. The source app collects the selected node, required node schema, markdown content, origin identity, and any relation or asset dependencies valid to share under the Obsidian reference rules.
>   * 4\. The source app ensures the selected node and required dependency records are persisted through the normal local-to-remote sync contract.
>   * 5\. The source app grants access to the chosen group through shared persistence.
>   * 6\. Later local edits to the shared source node are propagated by the existing local-to-remote sync model; the user does not need to re-share unless the target group changes.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC2: Destination user discovers cross-app shared nodes

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user opens an import surface after being granted access to shared content from the other app.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The destination app queries visible shared resources.
>   * 2\. Nodes from the other app appear with source app, source space, title, source-local ID, and modified time.
>   * 3\. Already imported nodes are hidden or marked using stable origin identity.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC3: Obsidian user pulls Roam-origin nodes into a vault

> * **Actor:** Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Roam-origin nodes from the import UI.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The Obsidian plugin fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2\. The plugin materializes each Roam node as a markdown file under an import folder, with mapped , stable , and frontmatter.
>   * 3\. The plugin imports relations where both endpoints resolve locally, then reports import successes and failures.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC4: Roam user pulls Obsidian-origin nodes into a graph

> * **Actor:** Roam user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Obsidian-origin nodes from the Roam import surface.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The Roam extension fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2\. The extension materializes each Obsidian node into Roam using the v0 markdown payload and Roam's markdown import/from-markdown capability.
>     * And changes to existing nodes are overwritten
>   * 3\. The extension stores stable origin identity so the imported node can be recognized and refreshed later.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC5: Destination user refreshes an imported cross-app node

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** An imported node has changed upstream and the destination user explicitly asks for the latest shared version.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The destination app identifies the source app, source space, and source-local node ID from stored origin identity.
>   * 2\. The destination app fetches the latest shared markdown content and metadata.
>   * 3\. The destination app updates the existing imported node without creating a duplicate and refreshes source timestamps.
>   * Any changes to the imported node are overwritten.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC6: Relation between separately shared nodes is preserved

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The source user shares a discourse node that has a stored discourse relation to another node already shared to the same group.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. The source app confirms both relation endpoints are shared to the same group.
>   * 2\. The source app writes the relation type schema and relation instance into shared persistence using the same semantic shape Obsidian imports today.
>   * 3\. The destination app maps or creates the local relation type and materializes the relation if both endpoints resolve locally.
>   * 4\. The destination app imports cross-app relation instances as tentative/unaccepted by default.
>   * 5\. Roam stores tentative relation state on the stored/reified relation record
>   * 6\. Tentative Roam relations are shown or discoverable separately from accepted local relations.
>   * 7\. A Roam user can accept or remove a tentative relation. Acceptance promotes it to the normal local relation set.
> * **Version:** MVP0

>>>

>>> ### UC7: Markdown content is later replaced by canonical atJSON

> * **Actor:** Engineer
> * **Trigger:** MVP0 is working and the team is ready to improve cross-app content fidelity.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1\. Roam and Obsidian adapters convert app-native content into a DG-owned atJSON-compatible document.
>   * 2\. Destination adapters render that canonical document into the destination app's native local representation.
>   * 3\. The same canonical content can later render to Roam, Obsidian
> * **Version:** v1

input.description:
## Problem

* Sid published Evidence from Roam and MG imported it into Roam. The Source was published and listed in the discovery dialog, but the import reported "No source was published with this node." The imported title shows `[[@placeholder]]` and the Source was not imported.
* Publishing Evidence before its Source is in this space's database drops the source reference (`omitMissingSource` in `publishNodesToGroups.ts`). Publishing the Source later does not restore it. Only publishing the Evidence again restores it.
* ENG-2293 expects an accessible published Source to import with its Evidence. This publish order breaks that.

## Solution

* When a Source is published, re-upsert the nodes in this space that name it as their source and were stored without a source reference.

## Done When

* Publishing Evidence, then its Source, stores the Evidence's source reference. Importing that Evidence into Roam imports the Source and resolves the title without the "No source was published with this node." warning.
* Publishing a Source does not publish or grant access to any other node.
* Publishing Evidence whose Source is not in this space still shows the missing-source warning and omits the reference.
* Unit tests cover the Evidence-then-Source publish order.

## Out of Scope

* Automatically publishing a Source with its Evidence.
* MAP's report that an Obsidian source gets filtered out when importing in Roam and Obsidian. Track it in a separate ticket.

## Notes

* Reported in the 2026-09-25 testing session. Screenshots: [imported Evidence](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FTHX_sIRj-o.png?alt=media&token=9c02ff04-4bd6-4f54-aa57-63a4492ea051), [import warning](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FQ8iRyQI9dR.png?alt=media&token=c2114c76-7b7a-4eaa-b598-67903e6b1693), [second imported Evidence](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FTV9_MzLHok.png?alt=media&token=5830617a-7da3-469c-ab94-459a272408ba).
* The publish order in the reported tests is unconfirmed. The observed warning matches the Evidence-first path.
* Obsidian already repairs this case during full sync (`findStaleSourceSlotNodeIds`).
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

# Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.

Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.

Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.

Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

## Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:

```typescript
// ❌ Unclear and inline
const result = items.filter(
  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
);

// ✅ Clear and reusable
const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
};

const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
};
```

- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:

```typescript
  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
  // Check if user can access premium features
  const check = (user: User) => { ... }

  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
```

- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:

```typescript
// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  // 30 lines of validation
  // 20 lines of transformation
  // 15 lines of formatting
};

// ✅ Composed of focused functions
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
};
```

## Documentation

- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Code hygiene

- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.

## Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

# Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.

Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.

Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.

Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

## Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:

```typescript
// ❌ Unclear and inline
const result = items.filter(
  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
);

// ✅ Clear and reusable
const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
};

const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
};
```

- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:

```typescript
  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
  // Check if user can access premium features
  const check = (user: User) => { ... }

  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
```

- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:

```typescript
// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  // 30 lines of validation
  // 20 lines of transformation
  // 15 lines of formatting
};

// ✅ Composed of focused functions
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
};
```

## Documentation

- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Code hygiene

- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.

## Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

---
name: dg-pr-adherence-check
description: Review a PR or local diff for adherence to Discourse Graphs code standards and PR requirements, report concerns to the author, and return a Standards check checkbox. Use before handoff or requesting review, alongside scope-check.
---

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.
SKILL.md

---
name: pre-pr-review
description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
user_invocable: true
---

<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)

Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)

If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:

- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)

## Step 4 — Process gate

- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.
- Runtime proof: does this change have a surface a unit test can't exercise (UI, load-order, multi-user)? If yes, a demo is REQUIRED, not noted (`/demo-handoff`). If the diff touches DOM observers, drag/hover interactions, or rendered Roam surfaces: emit a **regression matrix** — surfaces (main window, right sidebar, left sidebar, Kanban, query-builder link/embed/render views, canvas) × content shapes (single-line, multiline/wrapping, nested references, page titles) — marking which cells this change can affect; the demo must drive every affected cell, with the mouse cursor visible in the recording, and any bug you claim fixed must be re-driven by you after the fix. Video quality bar (#1298): signal each state change visually (a quick caption/toast — "before fix" / "on branch"), don't carry it in narration alone, and cut narration that states the obvious ("every relation has a source and destination" earned a 🙄 from mdroidian).
- Reviewer context: list the bullets the PR description must contain (what was removed and why, temporary code, decisions made, deferrals + tickets). Test: could someone review this without asking a question?
- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.

## Output

1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.
2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.
3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.
</skill-prompt>

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)

- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).

- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.

- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.

## Output

1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.

Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). 2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.

content.content:
graph-data pitfalls (node formats, malformed relations, tldrawApps
     seeding) are in the README's "Canvas (tldraw) demos in Roam" section.
   - Probe graph data the demo depends on (node type formats, relation
     definitions) with a small headless roamSession script BEFORE the
     first recording — a title that doesn't match a node type's format
     fails silently (no relations, no node match).
   - UI gated behind a feature flag reads the flag at extension load, so
     the flag must already be persisted in the graph before the demo run.
     Persist it once with a one-scene util storyboard run with
     `--no-extension` (`util-enable-sync-flag.ts` and
     `util-enable-node-sharing-flag.ts` are templates — they mirror
     setFeatureFlag by writing props on the "Feature Flags" block of
     `roam/js/discourse-graph` and verify the read-back). Toggling the
     flag mid-storyboard does nothing without a reload.
   - An extensionAPI SETTING (setSetting / extensionAPI.settings.set) is a
     different animal from a feature flag and CANNOT be prepped once:
     recordDemo re-adds the developer extension each run and Roam drops the
     extension's settings with it, so the setting is back to its default at
     the start of every take (verified: set true in one run, reads false in
     the next). The extension API is module-scoped and not on `window`, and
     Roam's copy is a transit-encoded `graphAppState` localStorage blob, so
     a `js` step cannot write it either. Drive the settings panel in a first
     scene with `toast:` and no `caption:`, and assert the control afterwards
     so a silent failure surfaces there, not as a mystery timeout later
     (template: `storyboards/eng-1869.ts` scene 1). Beware settings whose
     switch opens a confirm dialog — "Enable stored relations" offers
     "Migrate again and Reactivate", which runs migrateRelations() and
     promotes tentative relations; take "Reactivate without Migration".
   - Blueprint checkboxes/switches: click
     `label.bp3-checkbox .bp3-control-indicator` (or the label), never the
     `input` — the indicator intercepts pointer events and a click on the
     input burns the full timeout with
     "<span class=\"bp3-control-indicator\"> intercepts pointer events".
     Reading `input.checked` in a `js` step is still fine.
   - A title-additions button (`handleTitleAdditions`) shares the
     `.discourse-graph-title-additions` container with other title
     buttons (e.g. Share appears when the title matches a node format) —
     anchor selectors with `:has-text("...")`, never bare `button`.
3. Seed test data idempotently inside the storyboard's first scene (`js`
   action with roamAlphaAPI); recreate pages that must be clean each run.
   - EXCEPTION — discourse node TYPES: the dev graph runs the LEGACY
     settings store, so a seeded `discourse-graph/nodes/<label>` page needs
     BOTH the config tree (Shortcut/Tag/Format child blocks — what the
     settings panel and discourseConfigRef read) and block props (what the
     new store reads), written the way createDiscourseNodeType does. Props
     alone render an empty row. And the config cache builds at extension
     load, so seed node types with a standalone pre-recording session
     (template: `storyboards/eng-2055.prep.ts`, seed/cleanup modes with
     fresh-session verification), not in scene 1.
   - Cleaning up "pages my feature created" is not enough when a step can
     collide by title (import refuses a title an unrelated local page
     holds) — delete by the titles the demo will create too.
   - If a scene must move state the app only reads (e.g. a shared row in
     Supabase standing in for an edit made in another app), do it from the
     storyboard so takes stay repeatable: interpolate
     `process.env.<KEY>` into the `js` string and run the recorder after
     `set -a; . packages/database/.env.local; set +a`. Never commit keys
     into a storyboard. Details in the README.
4. Add `js` assertions after key scenes — storyboards double as regression
   tests, and a red run before the fix / green after is reviewer gold.
5. Record (from `discourse-graph/apps/roam`):
   `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/recorder/recordDemo.ts
   --storyboard <file> --narrate --cursor` (always headed on workspace 9;
   add `--allow-login` once if the profile session expired).
   - `--cursor` burns a visible cursor (arrow overlay + click ripple, and
     clicks glide to the target instead of teleporting) so the viewer sees
     where each action happens. When it's on, prefer clickable interactions
     in the storyboard over bare keypresses (click the menu item, don't
     press its hotkey) — a keypress leaves the cursor idle while state
     changes.
   - Before launching, run `pgrep -af "loadExtension.ts|recordDemo.ts"`:
    another worktree's live-test loader holds a slot just like a recorder
    does. Wait for it to exit (never kill it); if the first launch still
    says "Opening in existing browser session", the lock was clearing, so
    rerun once.
  - Parallel-session contention is at the PROFILE SLOT, not the workspace:
     Playwright screencast captures the page, so two recorder windows can
     share workspace 9 without polluting each other (only recordDuo's
     x11grab needs the screen exclusively). If launch fails with "Opening
     in existing browser session", another session holds slot 1 — never
     kill its Chromium; rerun with `--slot 3 --url <graph-url>` (only slot
     1 has GRAPH_URL in apps/roam/.env). If that slot's profile isn't
     logged in, clone the logged-in one: `cp -a playwright-1 playwright-3`
     under `discourse-graph/local/roam-playwright/profiles/` (read-only for
     the running slot; Roam's login is IndexedDB inside the profile).
   - "Roam profile is not logged in or the session expired" has two causes
     and they need different responses; never reach for `--allow-login` (and
     never type credentials) before telling them apart. waitForRoamReady
     waits 1.5s then fails on a `#/signin` URL, but Roam redirects there
     before restoring the session from the profile's IndexedDB. Diagnose:
     watch the window title via `i3-msg -t get_tree` ("Daily Notes - Google
     Chrome for Testing" = that run reached a logged-in graph; stuck at
     "about:blank" = it never did), check `uptime`, and run `pgrep -af "npm
     exec tsx"` for another worktree's recorder or diagnostic competing for
     CPU and disk (a different profile slot still contends). Filmstripping
     `<output>-failed.webm` is weak evidence: it only covers the first
     seconds, so blank frames do not distinguish the two.
     Transient — high load or a parallel session, other runs still reach
     Daily Notes: wait for quiet and rerun. Real logout — every run
     redirects with the machine idle: suspect concurrent use of the same
     Roam account, since slot 3's profile is usually a `cp -a` clone of slot
     1 and driving both can invalidate the shared session. That one needs a
     human sign-in; hand it to sid rather than retrying (six failed runs in
     one session before the pattern was clear).
   - `--workspace <n>` moves ONLY this run's window off workspace 9 after
     launch (window ids are snapshotted around launch, so a parallel
     recording's window is never touched). Use it when two headed runs on
     ws9 would confuse whoever is watching; the target workspace must stay
     visitable (an occluded window can throttle rendering).
   - A one-off `launchPersistentContext: Timeout 180000ms` with the browser
     visibly rendering (frame-latency stderr spam) has happened; clear the
     profile's stale `Singleton{Lock,Cookie,Socket}` symlinks (only when no
     chromium is actually running) and rerun — the retry succeeded.

## Feature demo (Obsidian, or any Electron app, over CDP)

Playwright can't `recordVideo` a CDP-attached app, so `recordObsidian.ts`
captures a screenshot loop with real timestamps and assembles via ffmpeg
concat; captions/narration work like recordDemo. Same storyboard shape
(actions: click/type/fill/press/pause/wait_for/js/screenshot).

0. Build the plugin with the local DB and the embeddings stub baked in
   (`SUPABASE_USE_DB=implicit NEXT_API_ROOT=http://127.0.0.1:3210 pnpm run
   build` from the worktree's `apps/obsidian` after exporting
   `packages/database/.env.local`; `grep -c 127.0.0.1:54321 dist/main.js`
   → 1), stage it in `/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-XXXX/`, back up and
   install `main.js` + `styles.css` into the vault's plugin folder, and start
   `recorder/embed-stub.py` before launching. README "Obsidian builds for
   demos" has the details; the previously installed plugin had no DB env.
1. Launch the app with debugging (AppImages need `--no-sandbox` when the
   SUID sandbox errors): `~/Applications/Obsidian.AppImage --no-sandbox
   --remote-debugging-port=9223 &`, then poll `http://127.0.0.1:9223/json`.
   Obsidian opens the LAST-OPEN vault — set the target vault's
   `"open": true` in `~/.config/obsidian/obsidian.json` first, and restore
   it during cleanup. If an Obsidian instance is already running, stop and
   ask — never kill the user's instance.
2. Record (from `discourse-graph/apps/roam`):
   `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/recorder/recordObsidian.ts
   --storyboard <file> --narrate [--cdp http://127.0.0.1:9223]`
3. Obsidian command palette is `Control+p` → `.prompt input`; DG import
   modal is `.modal` with `text=Select nodes to import`. Escape resets a
   half-open modal between runs.
4. Never actually import/mutate in the demo unless asked — end with Cancel.

## Recording on a tiling WM (i3)

The desktop here is i3 — new windows get tiled to arbitrary sizes, and a
human can accidentally close/resize the headed window mid-run. Rules:

- HEADLESS IS FORBIDDEN — sid's standing rule: every recording must run
  headed and visible on screen (recordDemo.ts now ignores `--headless`
  with a warning; never try to re-enable it). Tell sid which workspace to
  watch, and that the window must not be focused/resized mid-run.
- Workspace 9 is the standing home for ALL recorder windows. The i3 config
  has `for_window` rules: `class="(?i)obsidian"` → move to ws9;
  `class="Chromium-browser"` (Playwright's Chromium — NOT `Chromium`,
  verify with a probe if unsure) → move to ws9 + **floating enable**.
  Never launch a headed window onto the user's active workspace; if a rule
  is missing for a new app class, add it + `i3-msg reload` BEFORE launching.
- Headed screencast captures the WINDOW scaled into the canvas, so the
  window's CSS size must EQUAL the viewport or the video shows a shrunken
  page in a gray frame. Floating (not tiled, not fullscreen) lets
  Playwright size the window exactly; `recordDemo.ts --dpr 2` (default)
  forces device-scale 2 for retina-sharp 720p-layout → 1080p output, and
  `--dpr 1` records big fixed-layout pages natively.
  `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` still pins CDP-attached Electron
  capture (recordObsidian) regardless of tile size.
- NEVER call CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds` under a tiling WM — i3 fights
  it and the call can hang the whole run (this froze a session once).

## Run recordings so they can't stall the session

Feature demos take ~1 min; anything longer means a hung selector, not a
slow run. Launch recorder commands in the background with output to a log file,
poll the log for `Scene x/y` progress, and tell the user which scene is
running. `recordObsidian.ts` has a built-in watchdog (~90s/scene) that
kills a stuck run; for `recordDemo.ts` set a Bash timeout (≤5 min) so a dead
run surfaces as a visible failure instead of silence. Distinguish hung
from slow by whether `Scene x/y` lines keep advancing in the log.

## Verify before sharing

## Run recordings so they can't stall the session

Feature demos take ~1 min; anything longer means a hung selector, not a
slow run. Launch recorder commands in the background with output to a log file,
poll the log for `Scene x/y` progress, and tell the user which scene is
running. `recordObsidian.ts` has a built-in watchdog (~90s/scene) that
kills a stuck run; for `recordDemo.ts` set a Bash timeout (≤5 min) so a dead
run surfaces as a visible failure instead of silence. Distinguish hung
from slow by whether `Scene x/y` lines keep advancing in the log.

content.text:
The fix is committed and in draft PR #1493, and the independent `/pre-pr-review` is still running. The PR isn't finished: that review, the video, and the last PR body checkboxes are still pending.

**Ticket:** [ENG-2329](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2329/restore-the-source-reference-when-a-source-is-published-after-its), "Restore the source reference when a Source is published after its Evidence in Roam". It's in `Ticket Draft` with the `Created by Claude`, `Roam plugin`, `Bug` and `Inter-Graph` labels, and it's linked to ENG-2293. It needs your review before it moves to `Backlog`. MAP's Obsidian report is listed as a separate follow-up under Out of Scope.

**Cause:** If Evidence is published before its Source is in the database, the publish drops the Evidence's link to the Source. Publishing the Source afterwards never put it back, so the import found no source and showed "No source was published with this node." You weren't sure of the publish order in the tests. This order matches the warning in your screenshots, and a unit test reproduces it.

**Fix** (`apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts`): when a Source is published, the plugin looks for Roam pages whose title names that Source. For each one already stored in this graph's database with its source link missing, it rewrites just that node's stored record (not its content) so the link points at the Source.
- It doesn't publish anything else or give anyone new access.
- Nodes that were never stored stay out of the database, so nothing unpublished gets uploaded.
- It only runs when the node being published is a Source, so publishing other nodes costs nothing extra.
- The "Source … is not in this space yet" warning no longer tells people to publish the Evidence again.
- Republishing "@trang test source page" should fix the Evidence already broken in your dev graph, though I haven't tried it live.

**Checks**
- `pnpm ci:validate` passes (types in all 8 packages, 598/598 Roam tests).
- eslint, prettier and tsc pass on both changed files.
- The new test fails when the fix is switched off.
- eslint reports one warning (an unused `eslint-disable` line). It's already on `main` on a line I didn't touch, so I left it.

**Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/eng-2329` now has its own frozen `pnpm install`. The borrowed `node_modules` from the main checkout pointed at an older copy of `@repo/database` and caused 6 false test failures. The install reset the shared hooks path, which I set back to the absolute path.

**Next:**
- When the review returns, I'll fix or answer its findings.
- Then I'll fill in the PR's Scope check (none beyond Done When), Standards check and Local delegated full review sections.
- Then a subagent records the video. Your graph can't list its own published nodes for import, so it needs a second Roam graph. It will show before and after: the Evidence stored without its source link, publishing the Source restores it, and importing into the second graph brings in the Source with the real title.

I updated my saved note on videos to say a subagent may record one when you ask for it here.
